subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost focus
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@fintechinc.com>; Priya Shah <priya@fintechinc.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost focus

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time to chat today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points you shared
- Inference unit economics are the top constraint: current spend is outpacing revenue growth and makes experimentation expensive.
- High variability in per-request token counts (user prompts + long contexts) which spikes cost unpredictably.
- Current setup has limited batching/caching capabilities due to the vendor API and your home-grown queuing layer.
- You’re open to quantization but need to balance cost vs any measurable quality regression on core flows.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Primary: Hosted API from a major provider for most features.
- Heavy batch/throughput: internal GPU pool on AWS (p3/p4) for high-volume jobs.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes + custom FIFO queue; limited observability into per-route token costs.

Success criteria you listed
- Reduce inference cost per 1M tokens by 40% vs current baseline while keeping top-line accuracy within 2% of current model quality.
- 95th percentile tail latency <= 450ms for interactive routes.
- Clear unit economics model for forecasting and cost alerts.

Immediate next steps
1) We’ll share a short baseline cost model template to capture your current token volumes, model mix, and infra rates (attached: fintech-cost-model.xlsx).
2) Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer to align on batching/caching constraints — suggested times below.
3) Prepare a short POC proposal (Dedicated or Private deployment) that targets quantization (int8) + batching to hit the cost target.

Suggested slot for technical deep-dive: Wed 11 Feb 10:00–10:45 PT or Thu 12 Feb 14:00–14:45 PT — let me know what works.

Attachments: fintech-cost-model.xlsx (baseline template)

Thanks again — Ben
Ben Carter

From: Alex Rivera <alex@fintechinc.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@fintechinc.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 17:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — inference cost focus

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A few clarifications and extra context:

- Cost baseline: I attached our current month export (summary tab) into the fintech-cost-model.xlsx you sent and added a sheet with raw request distributions. We see that 20% of our users generate ~60% of tokens due to long-form inputs.
- Latency: interactive routes are most sensitive; anything above ~500ms starts to impact conversion. Background/async jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Quantization: our ML lead is open to int8 but we’ve seen subtle hallucination spikes when we went more aggressive in earlier tests; so we want an approach that can be A/B'd against quality metrics (F1/ROUGE/whatever applies).
- Compliance: we need SOC 2 evidence and basic controls for PII handling; not strictly blocking for POC but required for production.

We’re good to do Wed 11 Feb 10:00 PT. Laura — thanks in advance for joining the deep-dive.

Alex Rivera
Head of Product, FinTech Inc
alex@fintechinc.com | (212) 555-9101

1) Baseline cost model: I reviewed your numbers and will return a populated baseline that models three approaches — Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated pool, and Private deployment — with estimated per-1M-token cost, expected latency ranges, and infra assumptions. Expect that by EOD Tue 10 Feb.
2) POC scope: propose a 4-week POC focused on a single interactive route that represents ~30% of tokens but ~60% of your conversions. Technical goals: enable batching/caching, deploy an int8-quantized variant, and instrument SLO/quality checks.
3) Technical deep-dive: confirm Wed 11 Feb 10:00–10:45 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite to lock it. Please have your ML engineer (recommended) and infra engineer on the call so we can map batching constraints and KV cache integration.

A couple of questions to prep the deep-dive:
- Do you have per-route peak concurrency numbers and typical sequence-length distribution exports we can look at?
- Any hard constraints on token retention / cache TTLs for privacy?

Thanks — Ben
